newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-JACKSON GRAND SLAMS RED SOX AS TWINS WIN 11-5.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-JACKSON GRAND SLAMS RED SOX AS TWINS WIN 11-5.

text.p: Darrin Jackson hit a grand slam and drove in six runs in his first game of the season as the Minnesota Twins coasted to an 11-5 rout of the Boston Red Sox, who lost their seventh straight game on Friday.
Jackson, recalled from Triple-A Salt Lake earlier in the day, doubled in two runs in the third.
"I never had a start like this before, this is one of those nights that nobody expects to happen," Jackson said. "I was real fortunate and came through."

In Kansas City, Deivi Cruz's RBI single in the top of the ninth snapped a 2-2 tie and Melvin Nieves capped an eight-run inning with a three-run homer to lead the Detroit Tigers to a 10-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
Justin Thompson won his third straight game, going eight innings. He allowed four hits and two runs to improve to 2-0 lifetime against the Royals.
Nieves and Damion Easley each had three RBI for the Tigers, who banged out 14 hits but left 17 men on base.

At Texas, Julio Santana pitched four-hit ball over 6-1/3 innings, and Damon Buford broke up a scoreless tie with a two-run homer in the sixth inning as the Texas Rangers blanked the New York Yankees, 6-0.
New York's David Wells was pitching a perfect game until Billy Ripken doubled with one out in the sixth, and two batters later Buford hit his third home run of the season.
"I got it up and over the plate but he went out there and got it," Wells said. "You've got to tip your hat to Buford, he is a good hitter and good player."

In Toronto, Roger Clemens allowed a run in seven innings and won his seventh game to tie for the major-league, and Alex Gonzalez hit a two-run homer to lead the Toronto Blue Jays to a 5-2 victory over the Cleveland Indians.

Clemens (7-0) gave up six hits and three walks and struck out four to join Baltimore's Jimmy Key as the majors' only seven-game winners. Clemens has allowed one run or less in six of his eight starts this season.
"(Pitching coach) Mel (Queen) told me in the third I was sitting on my back leg," said Clemens. "I stood up and my ball got a little faster. We just hung on and persevered."
In Seattle, Scott Erickson pitched eight strong innings to win his seventh game of the season as the Baltimore Orioles beat the Seattle Mariners 6-3.
Erickson allowed three runs and five hits with four strikeouts and no walks.
Lenny Webster had three hits, including his first homer of the season, and Roberto Alomar had two hits and two RBI for the Orioles.
Dennis Martinez (1-4), who is considering retirement, had his longest outing of the year, lasting 7-1/3 innings, allowing five runs and eight hits.
In Anaheim, Chuck Finley tossed a five-hitter for his first win of the season and the Anaheim Angels hit three home runs in a 5-1 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers.

Finley (1-3) allowed one earned run, walked one and struck out five for his first win since last September 23rd and first complete game victory since he threw a six-hitter in a 7-0 win over the Milwaukee Brewers last July 27th.
Jim Edmonds, Luis Alicea and Dave Hollins homered for Anaheim, which extended its season-high winning streak to five
In Oakland, Tony Phillips and Frank Thomas had two hits and an RBI apiece and Wilson Alvarez pitched 6-2/3 strong innings as the Chicago White Sox posted a 6-2 victory over the Oakland Athletics.
Thomas hit his seventh home run of the season in the seventh inning and Phillips, Ray Durham and Albert Belle each had sacrifice flies for the White Sox.
